note: Thresholds are copied verbatim from the pre-registration and were not changed.

E1.pass_rule: Zero counterexamples in at least 10,000 property-test cases with unequal sizes and float32 inputs

E2.prediction: The float32 client path adds a bias the float64 bound misses
E2.pass_rule: A counterexample to the float64-only bound exists for float32 inputs, or the float32 term is shown to be below 1e-6 of the bound
E2.reading: The float32 path does add a deterministic bias of up to 3/16 of a quantisation unit per client. It never pushes a client error past one unit, so 2cn/T survives. Neither clause of the rule holds.

E3.prediction: The Hoeffding bound holds with independent client RNG and fails with a shared seed
E3.pass_rule: Empirical 99th percentile below the bound for n 4 to 256 with independent RNG, and a violation at n 256 with a shared seed
E3.note_n4: At n=4 the Hoeffding bound with d=64 and delta=0.01 is larger than the worst case bound 2cn/T, so the check there is weak.

M1.prediction: A two-round ReLU counterexample exists and the L2 convex theorem holds in tests
M1.pass_rule: Counterexample reproduced, zero violations of the L2 bound in at least 1,000 convex trials
